questions.q: What is a Picklist field, per this lesson?
options: A field restricted to a predefined list of values, configured per org
A field that can hold any free-form text
A field that automatically calculates its value from other fields
A field type that only exists on custom objects
questions.explain: Picklist fields like Case Status or Opportunity Stage restrict input to a fixed, org-configured list of values.

questions.q: Why does a Picklist's exact stored values matter so much to an analyst, per this lesson?
options: A filter or grouping written for one org's picklist values can silently miss or misread data in an org with different values
Picklists cannot be used in reports at all
Picklist values are identical in every Salesforce org by default
Picklists are always stored as Currency fields internally
questions.explain: Picklist values are configured per org, so an analyst must check the actual values rather than assume from past experience.

questions.q: What does a Lookup field do, per this lesson?
options: Stores a reference to a record on another object, like a Case pointing to its Contact
Calculates a value automatically from other fields
Restricts input to a fixed set of predefined values
Stores a monetary amount with a currency code
questions.explain: A Lookup field is a relationship field that points to a record on another object.

questions.q: What makes a Formula field different from a Text or Number field, per this lesson?
options: Its value is calculated automatically from other fields and can't be directly edited by a user
It can only ever hold the number zero
It is always a required field on every object
It cannot be included in any report
questions.explain: A Formula field's content is entirely dictated by its formula, unlike a field a user types a value directly into.

questions.q: Why does a Currency field carry a currency code, per this lesson?
options: Because the same numeric value can mean very different things across currencies, which matters in multi-currency orgs
Currency fields never actually store a numeric value
The currency code is purely cosmetic and never affects reporting
Only custom fields can be of type Currency
questions.explain: The lesson notes the currency code matters especially in multi-currency orgs, where the same number means different real amounts.
